description: A plan for how goods move through a place: the network that carries them, the bottlenecks and conflicts, and the improvements worth pursuing.
scope_notes: This is a standard-practice starting point — edit to your scope. Rename, delete and add records until the list matches the work your agency actually agreed to do.

Every date is calculated forward from the notice-to-proceed date you enter. The offsets are round numbers reflecting how this kind of work is usually sequenced — they are placeholders for a real schedule, not commitments.
Freight work depends on data held by private carriers and shippers. Where you cannot obtain it, say which questions remain unanswered rather than filling the gap with assumptions.
Communities next to freight facilities carry most of the impacts and are usually the least represented in freight planning. The engagement deliverable exists to make that a named task.

No jurisdiction is assumed. Review periods, required notices, hearings and the body that adopts the work are set where you are; none of them are stated here. Add the records your own process requires.
Nobody is assigned. Applying a template never puts a colleague's name on a deadline — assign the records yourself once the team is settled.
